text: R19.3 in plain words. WHAT: the new home for your node's log, one table inside node.db. Each row gets a number, seq (1, 2, 3 in the order written, never reused), and one column for each of the 23 fields found in your log, all allowed empty, so nothing is lost when the old file is imported. Every row is kept, as the log has always been. WHY HERE: it's the thing the move moves into. R19.4 (the indexes) sits on top of it, and R19.5 (the migration) fills it, so both wait on it. It doesn't wait on the backup to be BUILT, only to be USED: creating an empty table harms nothing, but copying the log in comes only after a backup exists. WHAT YOU'LL SEE when it's done: nothing yet. The table exists empty beside the working log until R19.5 moves the rows. STATE: decided (your 'i agree to the keys as well'), peer-reviewed by wsl, not built.

R19.4 in plain words. WHAT: three shortcuts into the new table, so the log's readers stop reading everything to find a few rows. (1) By hash: 'everything that happened to this message', a request and its reply, for byHash and taken. Rows without a hash are left out. (2) By time, over your relay's owner events only: 'owner notices since then'. (3) By time, over admitted incoming messages only: 'arrivals since then'. WHY HERE: an index belongs to a table, so it comes after R19.3, and it must exist before R19.5 fills the table, or the first reads after the move would be slower than today. WHAT YOU'LL SEE: nothing by eye. It's speed, measurable as how long a lookup takes before and after. STATE: decided, not built.
